incidents.title: Regional authorities report three dead and six injured after drone attack in Kropyvnytskyi
incidents.summary: Ukrinform and the Kyiv Post report a Russian drone attack on Kropyvnytskyi on 14 October 2026. The Kirovohrad regional military administration reported three deaths and six injuries in the city; these remain claims by an involved party.
incidents.impact: Ukrinform carried the regional administration's figures at 01:08 local time on 15 October 2026 (UTC+03:00): three dead and six injured in Kropyvnytskyi. The Kyiv Post, relayed by uazmi.com at 01:46, reports the same total, with five injured people treated in city medical facilities and one who refused hospitalisation, and describes damage to the grounds of a multi-storey residential building, windows and parked vehicles in the city. Damage to a transport enterprise and homes elsewhere in Kropyvnytskyi district, and in Oleksandriia district, is excluded from this city record.
incidents.evidence: Two separate news organisations, Ukrinform and the Kyiv Post, report this event. Both attribute the casualty figures to the regional military administration, so their agreement is not independent verification of the toll. Drone involvement remains reported. No social-media page was used as a source.
incidents.unknown: The final casualty total and the precise time of each strike are not established. The death toll rose during the night; the figure here is the total as of 15 October 01:08 local time, not a final count.
incidents.attribution: The cited Ukrainian reports attribute the attack to Russia. This attribution by an involved party has not been independently verified here.

incidents.title: Possible drone reports disrupt flights in Nuremberg
incidents.summary: Police reported possible drone sightings early on 13 October 2026. The airport operator reported precautionary disruption of flights. The reported object was not verified.
incidents.impact: As described in the airport operator’s report read on 13 October: six flights were delayed, comprising two arrivals and four departures; two arrivals diverted and subsequently continued to Nuremberg. Anadolu quotes police as saying reports occurred approximately 02:00–04:00 local time (CEST, UTC+02:00). These are sighting-report times, not a demonstrated two-hour closure interval.
incidents.evidence: The airport operator supplies its own account of operational disruption. Anadolu separately quotes police about reports from three pilots and the unsuccessful verification. These are separate reporting organisations and distinct operational observations, but the drone assertion shares the pilots’ reports; there are not two independent physical confirmations of a drone.
incidents.unknown: Whether the object was a drone, who operated it and the precise start and end of the precautionary flight suspension remain unresolved. The operator page displays 12 October while its body expressly identifies Tuesday 13 October; use the explicit event date, preserve the publication discrepancy. A later aircraft emergency is a separate reported event; no causal connection is established here.

incidents.title: Drones strike cargo ship Chelsea 3 off Byala, Bulgaria; crew of 15 rescued
incidents.place: Black Sea, about 18 nautical miles east of Byala (Bulgarian exclusive economic zone)
incidents.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the Maltese-flagged cargo ship Chelsea 3 was hit by three aerial drones about 18 nautical miles east of Byala, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea, during the night of 12 to 13 October 2026. All 15 crew members were rescued.
incidents.impact: The Border Police rescued all 15 crew members (seven Ukrainian and eight Azerbaijani nationals) and took them to Varna; five received treatment for minor injuries, according to BTA and BNT, while Sega reports six hurt, mostly with light burns. The ship, sailing empty from Giresun (Türkiye) to Giurgiulești (Moldova), stayed afloat and was at anchor.
incidents.evidence: Drone involvement rests on the statement of Bulgaria's prime minister, whose country is not a party to the war, and on the crew, who described three strikes on the deck and side. The national news agency BTA and the public broadcaster BNT report the statement; Sega adds the ship's route and management. A distress signal reached Bulgaria's maritime rescue centre at about 01:30 (Sega: 01:57). Sources give the distance as 15 or 18 nautical miles off Byala.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and from where is not established. The exact time of the strike is not given in the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: Not established. Radev said there was no solid, clear evidence against any party, while arguing that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation; he said he would summon Russia's ambassador for talks.

incidents.title: Cargo ship Azov Concord sinks off Krapets, Bulgaria, after drone attack
incidents.place: Black Sea, about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets (Bulgarian exclusive economic zone)
incidents.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said a second merchant ship, the Azov Concord, was hit and sank about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, in the same series of drone attacks in which the Chelsea 3 was struck off Byala on the night of 12 to 13 October 2026.
incidents.impact: The ship sank. BTA and BNT report one crew member rescued; Sega cites the Varna regional governor as saying four sailors were rescued in an operation northeast of Cape Shabla. According to Sega, the ship was flagged in St Kitts and Nevis, managed by a Turkish company and sailing from Romania to Türkiye.
incidents.evidence: Reported by Bulgaria's prime minister, whose country is not a party to the war, as one of the ships hit in the night's drone attacks; carried by the national news agency BTA, the public broadcaster BNT and Sega. The number of drones that hit this ship is not given.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones, how many hit the ship, the size of its crew and whether anyone is missing were not clear at the time of reporting. Maritime.bg, cited by Sega, placed the sinking east of Shabla rather than Krapets.
incidents.attribution: Not established. Radev said there was no solid, clear evidence against any party, while arguing that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation; he said he would summon Russia's ambassador for talks.

incidents.title: Coalition reports incoming drones and cruise missiles over Saudi Arabia after weekend airport strikes
incidents.summary: Early on Monday 12 October the Saudi-led coalition said it was tracking threats from drones and cruise missiles targeting the kingdom; Reuters reported that incoming drones and missiles were reported by the coalition, with no immediate news of whether they were intercepted. This followed strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on 10 and 11 October that the cited reports describe as a missile strike and an unidentified projectile, not as drone attacks.
incidents.impact: No impact from the drones reported on Monday 12 October is established in the cited sources.
incidents.evidence: Drones appear in this dossier only through the Saudi-led coalition's statements on Monday 12 October, as reported by Arab News and Reuters. Both relay the coalition, a party to the conflict, so they are not independent confirmations. The earlier airport strikes are not drone incidents in the cited sources: Reuters describes Saturday's deadly strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport as a missile strike, and GACA said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 on Sunday, killing a Pakistani national and injuring 11. GACA also said Dammam's King Fahd International Airport was targeted on Sunday evening, without naming the weapon. Those strikes are context only and are not attributed to drones here. Japanese broadcaster TBS, citing the Saudi-led coalition, reported that a drone hit a terminal at Riyadh's international airport on 11 October and caused a fire. That account comes from a party to the conflict and differs from GACA's statement (an unidentified projectile); it is shown as context, not as confirmation of a drone strike.
incidents.unknown: Where the reported drones were heading, how many there were, whether any were intercepted or reached a target, and who launched them are not established in the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: The cited reports do not say who launched the drones reported on Monday; they describe the alerts in the context of the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia. The Houthis claimed Saturday's airport attack, which the cited sources do not attribute to drones.

incidents.title: Drone strikes tanker Petro Dolphin off Sohar, Oman; two seafarers missing
incidents.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reclassified an incident at Sohar anchorage in Oman as an attack after confirming that a tanker was struck by a drone. India's shipping minister said nine of the 11 Indian crew members were rescued and two remain missing.
incidents.impact: India's minister of ports, shipping and waterways said the tanker carried 11 Indian nationals; nine were rescued and two remained missing while the local coast guard searched. A social-media post embedded by The Maritime Executive, citing preliminary information, gives 12 people on board (11 Indian nationals and one Bangladeshi national) with 10 rescued. That is compatible with the minister's figures if the non-Indian crew member was among those rescued, but it is not an official statement. UKMTO said damage and environmental impact were unknown at the time of its update.
incidents.evidence: Drone involvement was confirmed by UKMTO, the maritime security reporting centre, which first logged the incident as suspicious activity; 'confirmed' here means confirmed by UKMTO. Both cited articles relay the same UKMTO update and the same Indian ministerial statement, so they are not two independent confirmations. The Maritime Executive dates UKMTO's confirmation to Sunday 11 October; Reuters, via The Jerusalem Post, reported it on Monday 12 October. The Indian government identified the vessel as the Petro Dolphin, a small product tanker.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drone is not established in the cited sources; The Maritime Executive describes it as the latest suspected Iranian strike, without official attribution. The fate of the two missing seafarers and the extent of the damage were not known at the time of reporting.
incidents.attribution: Not established in the cited sources.

incidents.title: Russian drones enter Polish airspace overnight; Poland and NATO allies shoot some down
incidents.place: Eastern and central Poland, including the Lublin region
incidents.summary: Overnight on 9 to 10 September 2025, drones entered Polish airspace during a Russian wave of strikes on Ukraine. Poland's prime minister told parliament that 19 violations were recorded over seven hours. Polish and Dutch aircraft, supported by other NATO assets, shot down some of the drones. Poland called it an act of aggression and consulted allies under Article 4 of the NATO treaty.
incidents.impact: Part of Poland's airspace was closed for several hours and Warsaw's Chopin Airport suspended flights. A house in the village of Wyryki in the Lublin region was damaged and its roof largely torn off; the people inside were not hurt. Drones were found at seven locations, and objects of unknown origin at an eighth.
incidents.evidence: Polish authorities recorded the violations and recovered drones at multiple sites, and a NATO spokesman said NATO planes engaged potential threats in allied airspace. Figures differ between sources: 19 violations over seven hours according to the prime minister on 10 September, and 21 drones detected with at least three shot down in the Arms Control Association's later summary.
incidents.unknown: Whether the incursion was intentional. Russia's Defense Ministry said it did not target Poland, and Belarus said it tracked drones that lost their course after jamming, while several European leaders said it appeared intentional. The exact number of drones and of those shot down is not settled, and the cause of the damage to the house (drone debris or an interceptor) is described differently.
incidents.attribution: Polish authorities and NATO officials treated the drones as Russian, and the Arms Control Association reports that debris analysis by multiple media outlets and Polish authorities indicates Russian origin, likely Gerbera-type drones. A joint statement by the foreign ministers of Poland, Lithuania and Ukraine on 12 September accused Russia of a deliberate and coordinated strike. Russia denied targeting Poland, so responsibility for sending the drones into Polish airspace, and intent, remain disputed; recorded here as suspected.

incidents.title: Drone strike damages the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement; IAEA later finds it lost its confinement function
incidents.place: Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, Kyiv region
incidents.summary: At about 01:50 on 14 February 2025 a drone struck the New Safe Confinement, the structure covering the destroyed Unit 4 reactor at the Chornobyl site, and caused a fire. The IAEA team at the site heard the explosion and saw a breach of the outer layer. In late 2025 the IAEA reported that the strike caused significant structural damage and that the structure had lost its primary safety functions, including confinement, without permanent damage to its load-bearing structures.
incidents.impact: No casualties were reported and radiation levels inside and outside the building stayed normal and stable. The IAEA later said the strike did not lead to any release of radioactive material but caused significant structural damage affecting the confinement function and projected lifetime of the structure. Limited temporary repairs were carried out on the roof, and further temporary repairs were planned for 2026 with support from the EBRD.
incidents.evidence: The IAEA team at the site heard the explosion, saw smoke, fire and the breach, and was informed by Ukraine that a drone had struck the structure. incidents.place: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar area
incidents.summary: On 7 April 2024 drones struck the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, the first direct targeting of the plant since November 2022 according to the IAEA. The IAEA's director general reported at least three direct hits against the main reactor containment structures, and on 9 April another drone detonated on the roof of the plant's training centre outside the site perimeter. Russia and Ukraine blamed each other.
incidents.impact: The IAEA said damage at unit 6 did not compromise nuclear safety but was a serious incident with potential to undermine the integrity of the reactor's containment system, and one casualty was reported. Russia's state nuclear agency said three people were wounded. The plant's six reactors had been shut down for months.
incidents.evidence: IAEA experts at the plant verified the impact of several drone attacks on 7 April, and on 9 April they heard a loud explosion at the time the plant said a drone detonated on the training centre roof. The IAEA team was denied access to several locations for security reasons. The director general later told the IAEA Board the strike did not compromise nuclear safety in a serious way.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and from where: the IAEA did not attribute the attacks. The drone type is not stated in the cited sources. The IAEA could not visit several of the locations where the plant reported attacks.
incidents.attribution: Plant officials said Ukrainian military drones carried out the attack, and Russia's IAEA ambassador accused the agency of being afraid to say Ukraine was behind it. Ukraine's UN ambassador called the strike a false flag operation by Russia. The IAEA director general said that whoever is behind the attacks is playing with fire and did not attribute them.

claims.statement: The IAEA confirmed physical impact of drone attacks at the plant, including at one of its six reactors.
claims.quote: In a separate statement, the IAEA confirmed physical impact of drone attacks at the plant, including at one of its six reactors.
claims.note: Confirmation by an international body whose team was on site; the basis for the confirmed drone status.

claims.statement: The IAEA director general confirmed at least three direct hits against the main reactor containment structures.
claims.quote: confirmed at least three direct hits against the ZNPP main reactor containment structures took place
claims.note: Statement posted on X and reported by AP.

claims.statement: The IAEA said damage at unit 6 had not compromised nuclear safety but was a serious incident that could undermine containment integrity.
claims.quote: Damage at unit 6 has not compromised nuclear safety, but this is a serious incident with potential to undermine integrity of the reactor's containment system
claims.note: Describes the limits of the damage as well as the risk.

claims.statement: On 9 April the IAEA team heard an explosion at the time the plant said a drone detonated on the training centre roof.
claims.quote: a loud explosion at 11:05am local time today, the same time that the ZNPP later said an incoming drone had detonated on the roof of the facility's training centre
claims.note: The IAEA corroborates the explosion and its timing, but could not access the building to assess the impact.

claims.statement: The IAEA director general did not name who was behind the attacks.
claims.quote: Whoever is behind them, they are playing with fire. Attacking a nuclear power plant is extremely irresponsible and dangerous, and it must stop
claims.note: Explicitly leaves the attacker unnamed.

claims.statement: Plant officials said the site was attacked by Ukrainian military drones, including a strike on the dome of the sixth power unit.
claims.quote: Officials at the plant said the site was attacked Sunday by Ukrainian military drones, including a strike on the dome of the plant's sixth power unit.
claims.note: Statement by the occupying side; the IAEA has not confirmed who launched the drones.

claims.statement: Ukraine's UN ambassador called the strike a false flag operation by Russia.
claims.quote: called the drone strike a “well-planned false flag operation” by Russia
claims.claimant: Ukraine's ambassador to the United Nations
claims.note: Counter-accusation by a party to the conflict, unverified.

timeline.text: Drones struck several buildings at the plant, including a direct hit on the reactor dome of Unit 6, according to the IAEA director general; plant officials blamed Ukrainian military drones.
The IAEA confirmed physical impact of drone attacks at the plant, including at one of its six reactors; one casualty was reported, and Rosatom said three people were wounded.
The IAEA team heard a loud explosion at 11:05 local time, when the plant said a drone detonated on the roof of the training centre outside the site perimeter.
At an emergency IAEA Board meeting requested by Russia and Ukraine the director general said the strike did not compromise nuclear safety in a serious way; both sides traded accusations.

incidents.title: Anti-junta forces say 29 drones targeted Naypyidaw military sites; junta says it shot down seven
incidents.place: Naypyidaw (military headquarters, Aye Lar air base and Naypyidaw International Airport)
incidents.summary: On the morning of 4 April 2024 anti-junta forces attacked the Myanmar capital Naypyidaw with drones in a rare strike on the military regime's stronghold. The shadow National Unity Government said 29 explosive-laden drones targeted the military headquarters and an air base. The junta said its air defences shot down seven drones near the airport and a township and that there was no damage or casualties.
incidents.impact: Accounts conflict. The National Unity Government said preliminary reports indicated there were casualties, while the junta said there was no damage or casualties. A source at the airport said it was temporarily closed and a drone carrying a bomb was defused, and a civilian witness quoted by Myanmar Now said the drones landed at the edge of the airport runway.
incidents.evidence: The attack is described by both sides: the junta displayed images of downed drones and said it had seized 13, and anti-junta groups published photos of the drones used. Casualty and damage claims come from the parties and are not independently verified; residents near the targeted sites told RFA they were unaware of the attacks.
incidents.unknown: How many drones were launched, whether any reached their targets, and whether anyone was hurt. The numbers claimed by the sides (29 launched; seven shot down; 13 seized) cannot be reconciled from the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: The shadow National Unity Government and the anti-junta Shar Htoo Waw's Kloud Drone Team, working with units of the People's Defence Force, claimed the attack. The junta did not name who launched the drones in the statements cited.

claims.statement: Radio Free Asia reported that rebel groups targeted the military headquarters and air base with 29 drones, according to the National Unity Government.
claims.quote: Rebel groups targeted the junta’s military headquarters and air base in Myanmar’s capital Naypyidaw with 29 drones on Thursday
claims.note: Claim by a party to the conflict; the figure of 29 drones is not independently verified.

claims.statement: The junta said four drones approaching the airport and three approaching a township were shot down and destroyed.
claims.quote: Four drones approaching Naypyidaw airport and three drones approaching Zayarthiri township in the capital "were successfully shot down and destroyed," the junta's information team said in a statement.
claims.note: The junta's own statement acknowledges drones, though it gives a smaller number than the opposition.

claims.statement: The junta statement claimed there were no casualties or damage to buildings.
claims.quote: The junta statement claimed that there were no casualties or damage to buildings resulting from the attack.
claims.claimant: Radio Free Asia, reporting the junta statement
claims.note: Conflicts with the National Unity Government's preliminary reports of casualties.

claims.statement: A civilian witness told Myanmar Now that the drones failed to reach their intended targets and landed at the edge of the airport runway.
claims.quote: the drones were unable to reach their intended targets and had “landed at the edge of the airport runway.”
claims.claimant: Civilian witness quoted by Myanmar Now, via Radio Free Asia
claims.note: Second-hand account of a single witness.

claims.claimant: Anonymous source at the airport, via AFP

incidents.title: Three US service members killed in one-way drone attack on Tower 22 outpost in northeast Jordan
incidents.place: Tower 22 logistics outpost, northeast Jordan near the Syrian border
incidents.summary: On 28 January 2024 a one-way attack drone struck a US logistics outpost known as Tower 22 in northeast Jordan, near the Syrian border. US Central Command said three US service members were killed and at least 34 were injured. It was the first attack on US forces in Jordan since the Israel-Hamas war began and the first in the region to kill US troops since then.
incidents.impact: CENTCOM said three US service members were killed and at least 34 injured, with eight evacuated from Jordan in stable condition; about 350 US Army and Air Force personnel were deployed at the base. Jordan's government said none of its own troops were hurt.
incidents.evidence: CENTCOM described a one-way attack UAS that impacted the base, and Jordan's government spokesperson said the attack was carried out by a drone. Reporting says it is unclear why air defences did not intercept the drone. The outpost is not publicly disclosed by Jordan.
incidents.unknown: Which group launched the drone and from where, and why it was not intercepted. The injury figure was expected to fluctuate as personnel received follow-on care.
incidents.attribution: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, a network of Iranian-backed Iraqi militias, claimed credit for the attack, according to Task & Purpose; The War Zone reports the group said it attacked other US bases in Syria and an Israeli naval facility, without naming Tower 22 in the statement it quotes. The US president said the attack was carried out by radical Iran-backed militant groups operating in Syria and Iraq and did not name a specific group.

claims.statement: US Central Command said three service members were killed by a one-way attack UAS that impacted a base in northeast Jordan.
claims.quote: On Jan. 28, three U.S. service members were killed, and multiple personnel were injured from a one-way attack UAS that impacted on a base in northeast Jordan, near the Syrian border.
claims.note: Official statement as reproduced by The War Zone; the basis for the confirmed drone status together with Jordan's statement.

claims.statement: CENTCOM raised the number of injured personnel to at least 34 and said it expected the figure to fluctuate.
claims.quote: the number of U.S. personnel with injuries has increased to at least 34 service members, but we expect this number to fluctuate as service members continue to seek follow-on care
claims.note: Updated official figure; an earlier report said 25 injured.

claims.statement: Jordan's government spokesperson expressed condolences over victims of an attack carried out by a drone.
claims.quote: expressed Jordan’s condolences to the United States over the victims of the attack, which was carried out by a drone, and wished the injured a speedy recovery
claims.note: A second government, not directly party to the militia campaign, confirming the weapon type.

claims.statement: Task & Purpose reports that the Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed credit for the attack.
claims.quote: Islamic Resistance in Iraq, a loose network of Iranian-backed Iraqi militias opposed to the United States, claimed credit for the attack.
claims.note: A claim by the group as reported by Task & Purpose. The War Zone quotes a statement by the group that lists other targets, so the claim for Tower 22 rests on this report.

claims.statement: The US president said the attack was carried out by radical Iran-backed militant groups operating in Syria and Iraq.
claims.quote: While we are still gathering the facts of this attack, we know it was carried out by radical Iran-backed militant groups operating in Syria and Iraq.
claims.note: Names a category of groups, not a specific group; the US had not outright accused a specific group at the time.

The US president blamed Iran-backed militant groups operating in Syria and Iraq and said the US would respond; Jordan said none of its personnel were wounded.

incidents.title: Nigerian military drone strike kills villagers at a religious gathering in Tudun Biri, Kaduna state
incidents.place: Tudun Biri village, Igabi area, Kaduna state
incidents.summary: A drone strike on the night of Sunday 3 December 2023 hit villagers gathered in Tudun Biri, in Kaduna state's Igabi area, to mark the Prophet Muhammad's birthday. Kaduna's governor said civilians were mistakenly killed by a drone targeting terrorists and bandits, and the army division commander was quoted as saying a routine army mission inadvertently affected community members. The president ordered an investigation.
incidents.impact: The National Emergency Management Agency said 85 bodies had been buried while the search continued. Amnesty International's Nigeria office said 120 people were killed, citing its workers and volunteers; VOA reported at least 87 killed and at least 60 injured. Dozens of wounded were evacuated for treatment.
incidents.evidence: Kaduna state officials and the army division commander, as quoted in a state ministry statement, described a mistaken drone strike during an army operation. The Nigerian Air Force said it carried out no operations in Kaduna that night and noted it is not the only force operating armed drones. Defence officials later said terrorists had embedded themselves in the village, which the governor criticised.
incidents.unknown: The final death toll (85 buried per the emergency agency, at least 87 per later reporting, 120 per Amnesty), the circumstances of the targeting error, and the findings of the presidential investigation. A Nigerian army spokesperson had not responded to requests for comment in the first reports.
incidents.attribution: The head of the army division in Kaduna was quoted by the state government as saying the army was on a routine mission against terrorists and inadvertently affected members of the community, and the governor described a drone targeting terrorists and bandits. The air force said it did not operate in Kaduna that night. Amnesty International accused authorities of putting out contradictory explanations.

claims.statement: The National Emergency Management Agency said 85 bodies had been buried while the search was ongoing.
claims.quote: 85 dead bodies have so far been buried while search is still ongoing
claims.note: Official figure on the day; later reporting by VOA gives at least 87 killed.

claims.statement: Amnesty International's Nigeria office said 120 people were killed.
claims.quote: Amnesty International’s Nigeria office said 120 people were killed in the attack, citing reports of its workers and volunteers in the area
claims.note: A higher toll than the official burial count; based on the organisation's own workers and volunteers.

claims.statement: The governor of Kaduna said civilians were mistakenly killed and wounded by a drone targeting terrorists and bandits.
claims.quote: said civilians were “mistakenly killed and many others were wounded” by a drone “targeting terrorists and bandits”
claims.note: State government statement confirming a drone and the mistaken targeting.

claims.statement: The army division head was quoted as saying the army's routine mission against terrorists inadvertently affected members of the community.
claims.quote: The Nigerian army was on a routine mission against terrorists but inadvertently [its actions] affected members of the community
claims.claimant: Head of the army division in Kaduna, quoted by the Kaduna State Ministry of Internal Security
claims.note: A state statement quoting the army, not a statement issued directly by the army; an army spokesperson had not commented in the first reports.

claims.statement: The Nigerian Air Force said it carried out no operations in Kaduna that night and is not the only force operating armed drones.

claims.note: Shows a dispute between state and federal accounts over why the village was targeted.

incidents.title: Air strike on Dedebit camp for displaced people in Tigray kills dozens, aid workers say; TPLF calls it a drone attack
incidents.place: Dedebit, northwest Tigray, near the Eritrean border
incidents.summary: An air strike on a camp for displaced people in Dedebit, in northwest Tigray near the Eritrean border, late on Friday 7 January 2022 killed at least 56 people and wounded 30, according to aid workers and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). The TPLF spokesman called it a drone attack by the federal government. The UN humanitarian office said the attack caused scores of civilian casualties, and aid agencies suspended operations in the area.
incidents.impact: Two aid workers told Reuters that at least 56 people were killed and 30 wounded, many of them children, and said the local authorities confirmed the toll. The UN humanitarian office told AFP the attack caused scores of civilian casualties, and it said humanitarian partners suspended activities in northwest Tigray because of the ongoing threat of drone strikes.
incidents.evidence: The death toll comes from aid workers who asked not to be named and from the TPLF, a party to the conflict; the UN office's statement confirms civilian casualties but gives no figure. Aid workers described an air raid, and the drone description comes from the TPLF spokesman.
incidents.unknown: The exact number of victims, the type of aircraft or weapon used, and the operator. The Ethiopian government, military and prime minister's office had not responded to requests for comment in the first reports.
incidents.attribution: The TPLF spokesman blamed the federal government's forces and called it a drone attack. Ethiopian federal authorities did not immediately comment on this strike and have denied targeting civilians during the conflict. The United States condemned the air raid, and the European Union cited the air attack in a statement without naming who carried it out.

claims.statement: A TPLF spokesman called the attack another callous drone attack by the prime minister's forces.
claims.quote: “another callous drone attack” by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s forces on a camp for Internally Displaced People (IDPs) in Dedebit had “claimed the lives of 56 innocent civilians”
claims.note: A claim by a party to the conflict; the basis for the reported drone status. The aid workers' accounts describe an air raid.

claims.statement: Aid workers and the TPLF said at least 56 people were killed and 30 wounded in an air raid on the camp.
claims.quote: At least 56 people have been killed and 30 others wounded in Ethiopia’s Tigray following an air raid on a camp for civilians displaced by the brutal conflict
claims.claimant: Aid workers and the TPLF, via Al Jazeera and Reuters
claims.note: Unnamed aid workers and a party to the conflict; the figure could not be independently verified in the report.

claims.statement: The UN humanitarian office told AFP the attack caused scores of civilian casualties.
claims.quote: The U.N. humanitarian office told the AFP news agency that the attack in the town of Dedebit had caused “scores of civilian causalities.”
claims.claimant: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
claims.note: Independent UN corroboration of civilian casualties without a figure. The quote keeps the source's spelling.

claims.quote: The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said Sunday that aid groups have suspended their operations in northwest Tigray.
claims.claimant: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
claims.note: Operational consequence of the strike and of the threat of further drone strikes.

incidents.title: Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq and Khurais facilities set ablaze in drone and cruise-missile attack; attribution disputed
incidents.place: Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, Saudi Arabia
incidents.summary: Early on 14 September 2019, fires broke out at Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq processing plant and the Khurais oil field. Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said both sites were targeted by drones, and the Houthis claimed the attack, saying they used 10 drones. UN sanctions monitors later referred to drones and land-attack cruise missiles being used in the attack.
incidents.impact: The Saudi Press Agency, citing the interior ministry, said Aramco's industrial security teams were dealing with fires at both sites, which were later reported under control. Two sources told Reuters that 5 million barrels a day of crude production had been affected, close to half of the kingdom's output. Saudi Arabia said on 3 October that it had fully restored oil output.
incidents.evidence: The use of drones rests on the Saudi interior ministry's statement, the Houthi claim and the UN monitors' report, which refers to drones and land-attack cruise missiles used on 14 September. The production figure comes from unnamed sources cited by Reuters rather than an official statement.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the attack and from where. The UN monitors said the sites were approached from the north rather than from Yemen in the south and doubted the Houthis' range; the UN Secretary-General reported being unable to corroborate Iranian origin of the weapons. The monitors were not tasked with identifying who was responsible.
incidents.attribution: The Houthis claimed responsibility. The United States, European countries and Saudi Arabia accused Iran, which denied involvement. A UN panel of sanctions experts concluded that the Houthi forces did not launch the attacks, and the UN Secretary-General reported that the UN could not independently corroborate that the missiles and drones were of Iranian origin. No attribution has been independently established.

claims.statement: Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said the fires began after the sites were targeted by drones.
claims.quote: The fires began after the sites were "targeted by drones," the Interior Ministry said in a statement carried by the state-run Saudi Press Agency.
claims.note: Official statement of the Saudi government, a party to the Yemen conflict; the basis for the drone status together with the UN monitors' wording.

claims.statement: UN investigators referred to the drones and land-attack cruise missiles used in the 14 September attack.
claims.quote: doubted that the drones and land-attack cruise missiles used in the September 14 attack “have a sufficient range to have been launched from Yemeni territory under the control of the Houthis.”
claims.claimant: UN Panel of Experts on Yemen
claims.note: Independent UN experts, as reported by Reuters via Al Jazeera, treat drones and cruise missiles as the weapons used; the basis for confirmed drone status.

claims.statement: Two sources told Reuters that 5 million barrels a day of crude production had been affected.
claims.quote: Two sources close to the matter told Reuters news agency that 5 million barrels a day of crude production had been impacted
claims.note: Unnamed sources, not an official statement; the fires themselves are confirmed by the interior ministry.

claims.statement: The Houthi military spokesman said the rebels launched 10 drones in a coordinated attack on the sites.
claims.quote: military spokesman Yahia Sarie said the rebels launched 10 drones in their coordinated attack on the sites
claims.note: Claim of responsibility by a party to the conflict, broadcast on the Houthis' Al-Masirah channel.

claims.statement: UN sanctions monitors said the Houthi forces did not launch the attacks, despite their claims.
claims.quote: That despite their claims to the contrary, the Houthi forces did not launch the attacks on Abqaiq and Khurais on 14 September 2019.
claims.claimant: UN Panel of Experts on Yemen
claims.note: Contradicts the Houthi claim. The monitors were not tasked with identifying who was responsible, so this is not an attribution to another party.

claims.statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that the UN could not independently corroborate that the missiles and drones were of Iranian origin.
claims.quote: the UN was “unable to independently corroborate” that missiles and drones used in the attacks “are of Iranian origin”
claims.note: Does not clear or implicate Iran; it states the limits of the UN's own verification.

claims.statement: The United States, European countries and Saudi Arabia accused Iran of being behind the attack; Iran denied it.
claims.quote: The United States, European countries and Saudi Arabia accused Iran of being behind the attack on Saudi Aramco oil plants in Abqaiq and Khurais
claims.claimant: United States, European countries and Saudi Arabia
claims.note: Accusations by governments; the dossier does not adopt them because the UN monitors did not establish responsibility.
